diagnostic_evidence.quote: The assumption \cref{eq:aspgap} essentially requires that the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$, which is, in fact, a necessary condition for the convergence of RSBL.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims a structural bound under the single condition 'the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed b'. The formal hypothesis is \cref{eq:aspgap} for a decomposition $\Lambda=\diagm\{\Lambda_1,\dots,\Lambda_d\}$ with every $\Lambda_i$ of size exactly $b$. Since \cref{eq:aspgap} minimises cross-block eigenvalue distances, it forces all copies of each eigenvalue to lie in one block, i.e. the multiplicity groups must pack into $d$ bins of capacity $b$. Maximal multiplicity $\le b$ does not imply this: for $b=3$, $d=2$ and target spectrum $\{0,0,1,1,2,2\}$ (maximal multiplicity $2\le b$) any split of six eigenvalues into two triples splits some multiplicity group, so no decomposition makes \cref{eq:aspgap} positive and the theorem proves nothing, whereas the prose claims coverage.

failure_location.quote: Under mild spectral gap assumptions---specifically, the multiplicity of desired eigenvalues does not exceed $b$---we provide a structural bound for \cref{eq:defangle} when $\Omega$ is a Gaussian random matrix.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Narrow the scope statements to the true hypothesis: the bound applies when the target eigenvalues can be split into d groups of b with pairwise disjoint spectra (a packing condition strictly stronger than 'multiplicity at most b'), and say so explicitly.
issues.overall_effect: Target spectra whose multiplicity groups do not pack into blocks of size b (e.g. three doubly repeated eigenvalues with b=3, d=2, especially when the target cluster is spectrally isolated) fall outside the analysed regime although the introduction advertises them as covered.
issues.title: Advertised coverage 'multiplicity at most b' exceeds the hypothesis actually required
issues.why_classification: Every formal statement, its conclusion and its rate are unchanged and no proved regime is lost; only an informal scope gloss has to be made precise, a short local edit with no new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the quantity $\chim\chic$ defined in \cref{eq:defchi} is bounded by a constant depending on $b$ and $d$

issues.failure_explanation: The quantities on which \cref{eq:Gd} depends are not defined on the stated hypothesis set. (i) If a block $\Lambda_i$ has all b eigenvalues equal to $\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}$ (allowed, since within-block multiplicity up to b is exactly the advertised regime) then $\widehat B_i=\lambda_{\min}^{\cl}I$ and both numerator and denominator of the first ratio defining $\chim$ vanish, leaving 0/0. (ii) At d=1 the exponent 1/(d-1) in the definition of $\chic$ and in \cref{eq:Gd} is 1/0 and the minimum defining $\chic$ ranges over an empty index set; likewise the minimum in \cref{eq:aspgap} is over an empty index set at d=1, so the hypothesis '$\gap>0$' is meaningless although the paper explicitly invokes \cref{conj:chi} and \cref{conj:sb} at d=1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Declare each ratio defining chii_mono to be 1 when its denominator (and then its numerator) vanishes, and give the d=1 case of chi_coef, eq:Gd, eq:aspgap and conj:chi explicitly (chii_mono*chi_coef = 1, G_1 = 1, relative gap vacuous). All stated bounds survive unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The growth estimate \cref{eq:Gd} of thm:interpolation, the derived bound $G_d\le(\chim\chic/\gap)^{d-1}$, and the conjecture conj:chi are ill-defined for a full block of repeated eigenvalues at an endpoint of the cluster interval and for d=1.
issues.title: Growth quantities chii_mono/chi_coef and the relative gap are undefined in admissible degenerate configurations
issues.why_classification: Both failures are degenerate cases repaired by local conventions/definitions; the method, conclusions, rates and advertised regimes all survive with no new lemma or argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the probabilistic result for $c_{\Omega}$ comes directly from taking union bounds on the tail bounds above.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted rate is quantitatively false. Take d=2, m=3 (so n=3b and dn-bd^2=2b). Then c_Omega = sqrt(2b) max_{i<=2}||Omega_i^{-1}|| ||Omega_3||^2 ||Omega_3^{-1}||, and for b x b Gaussian blocks ||Omega|| and ||Omega^{-1}|| are both of order sqrt(b), so c_Omega^2 = Theta(b^5) with probability tending to one. The stated right-hand side is (2b)^3/delta^4 * (2 sqrt(b) + O(1)) = Theta(b^{7/2}/delta^4), which is smaller for all large b at fixed delta < 1/4. Hence the claimed 'with probability at least 1-4 delta' statement fails. Union-bounding the four norm factors, as the proof sketch prescribes, produces the fourth power of 2 sqrt(b) + sqrt(2 log(2(m-d)/delta)) (with the d and m-d allocations combining into (dn-bd^2)^3), not the first power.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the union bound over the four factors of c_Omega (allocating failure probabilities delta/(2d) and delta/(2(m-d)) to the Gaussian blocks) and state the resulting estimate c_Omega^2 <= const * (dn-bd^2)^3/delta^4 * (2 sqrt(b)+sqrt(2 log(2(m-d)/delta)))^4.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative high-probability control of c_Omega, i.e. the advertised probabilistic form of the structural bound, is unreliable and must be restated with a weaker rate.
issues.title: The high-probability bound on c_Omega^2 in thm:sb is false
issues.why_classification: The stated quantitative guarantee is false and cannot be preserved by any repair, so the rate must be weakened; the repair is a contained recomputation that keeps the same form of high-probability bound and loses no result, so the loss is limited rather than major.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that all eigenvalues in $\Lambda$ are contained in an interval $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$ and eigenvalues in $\Lambda_{\perp}$ are outside $[\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:boundMP bounds ||Phi(B_j)|| by sqrt(b) kappa(Omega_j) times the maximum of ||Phi(lambda)|| over the whole interval spanned by the spectrum of B_j. The proof replaces that maximum by the maximum over [lambda_min,lambda_max] \ [lambda_min^cl,lambda_max^cl], which is legitimate only if every block B_j has its spectrum inside one connected piece of that set. The hypotheses do not ensure this: nothing restricts the b x b block partition of Lambda_perp, so a block may contain eigenvalues both below and above the cluster interval; then the interval supplied by lem:boundMP contains the whole cluster interval, where an arbitrary matrix polynomial Phi can be far larger than on the exterior set. The inference is therefore invalid and eq:pfthmmain4, and with it eq:mainsb, do not follow from the cited lemma.

failure_location.quote: Note that all eigenvalues of $B_{j}$ for $d+1\leq j\leq m$ are in $[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\setminus [\lambda_{\min}^{\cl},\lambda_{\max}^{\cl}]$, \cref{lem:boundMP} yields that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the use of lem:boundMP by the sharper estimate obtained from its own proof with the maximum taken over the discrete spectrum, ||Phi(B_j)|| <= sqrt(b)||Omega_j^{-1}|| ||Omega_j|| max_{mu in spec(Lambda_j)}||Phi(mu)||; each such mu lies in the exterior set, so the displayed bound follows verbatim and eq:mainsb is recovered exactly.
issues.overall_effect: The main bound eq:mainsb of thm:sb is unproved as written for block partitions of Lambda_perp whose blocks straddle the cluster interval; every later claim built on thm:sb (conj:sb, cor:eig, cor:lr) inherits the gap.
issues.title: lem:boundMP does not yield the estimate used in the proof of thm:sb when a block straddles the cluster interval
issues.why_classification: The claimed estimate is true and follows from a short, local variant of the proof of lem:boundMP with the maximum taken over the spectrum instead of the enclosing interval; every claim, rate and regime is preserved, so the repair is routine rather than a new lemma.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: When $d = 1$, \cref{cor:eig} recovers the convergence result for randomized single-vector Lanczos method from \cite[Thm.~3.1]{kressner2024randomized}.

issues.failure_explanation: At d=1 the claimed right-hand side equals 1 for every n, while the left-hand side at ell=d is tan angle(range(Q),range(Omega)) with Gaussian Omega, i.e. ||K_perp K^{-1}|| with K = Q^T Omega and K_perp = Q_perp^T Omega; this is of order sqrt(nb) and hence larger than 1 with high probability for n large. What thm:sb combined with conj:chi actually yields is tan angle <= c_Omega (chi_mono chi_coef/gap)^{d-1}, and the n-dependent factor c_Omega cannot be absorbed into (c_{b,d,n}/gap)^{d-1} when d=1 (at d=1 the minimum defining gap is in addition over an empty index set). Thus the bound is false in the d=1 regime, cor:eig at ell=d inherits it, cor:lr inherits the misplaced constant, and the stated recovery of the randomized single-vector convergence result (which carries an n-dependent constant) does not hold.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bound with the n-dependent factor outside the power, e.g. tan angle(range(Q),K_d(A,Omega)) <= c_{b,d,n} (C_{b,d}/gap)^{d-1} with c_{b,d,n} bounding c_Omega as supplied by thm:sb, and adjust cor:eig and cor:lr to the same form.
issues.overall_effect: The conjectured cluster-robustness bound, its eigenvalue-computation corollary and its low-rank corollary are unreliable at d=1, the regime the paper explicitly advertises as recovering the single-vector theory; for d>=2 the constant can be absorbed and the rate is unaffected.
issues.title: The conjectured bound is false for d=1 and does not recover the single-vector theory
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee at d=1 (a constant-free bound) is false and cannot be preserved, so the conclusion must be weakened there and the statement form changed in three linked claims; the gap-rate gap^{1-d} and the advertised scope, including d=1, survive recognisably, so the loss is limited rather than major.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The results show that $\tan\angle (\range(Q),\mathcal{K}_{d}(A,\Omega))$ is independent of $\beta$.
The outcome demonstrates that for both exterior and interior eigenvalues, $\tan\angle (\range(Q),\mathcal{K}_{d}(A,\Omega))$ is proportional to $\gap^{1-d}$, consistent with \cref{conj:sb}.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated intervals the cluster for Lambda_k is centered at k(alpha+beta)/60 with half-width beta/60 (consistent with 'cluster radius beta/60'), so the edge-to-edge distance between clusters k and k+1 is (alpha-beta)/60, not alpha/60. As written, the relative gap of eq:aspgap therefore varies like alpha-beta and hence depends on beta; in the first experiment (alpha=1, beta from 2^{-1} to 2^{-12}) it varies by a factor of two, and the reported beta-independence of tan angle is incompatible with the simultaneously claimed scaling tan angle proportional to gap^{1-d} (a factor 2^{d-1} for d=5). Either the interval formula or the two stated parameter interpretations must be wrong, and under the literal formula the empirical check of conj:sb is mis-parameterised (the gap is overstated by the factor alpha/(alpha-beta)).

failure_location.quote: the absolute gap between nearby  clusters is $\alpha/60$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the interval formula so that the stated radius and gap both hold, e.g. use [alpha k + beta(2k-1), alpha k + beta(2k+1)]/60 (radius beta/60, gap alpha/60), and restate the measured relative gap as min cross-block distance divided by lambda_max - lambda_min; alternatively keep the formula and correct the gap to (alpha-beta)/60, which then requires reinterpreting the beta-independence claim.
issues.overall_effect: The description of the experimental setup and the interpretation of the empirical validation of conj:sb are unreliable: the gap values used in the claimed gap^{1-d} fit, and the claimed independence of the cluster radius, cannot both be correct for the stated parameterisation.
issues.title: Stated inter-cluster gap of the empirical parameterisation is wrong and conflicts with the reported beta-independence
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to the experimental parameterisation and its local interpretation; no theorem, bound or rate changes, and one local correction of the formula restores consistency with both stated parameter meanings and with conj:sb.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this simple situation, $\chim$ can be bounded using existing results from random matrix theory

issues.failure_explanation: For d=2 the only matrices entering chi_mono are B_1 and B_2, and the definition gives chi_mono(B_k;B_-k) = max{||lambda I - B_j||/||lambda I - Lambda_j||, 1} for lambda in {lambda_min^cl, lambda_max^cl}. Writing B_j = Omega_j^{-1} Lambda_j Omega_j, the ratio equals ||Omega_j^{-1}(lambda I - Lambda_j)Omega_j||/||lambda I - Lambda_j||, which is bounded by kappa(Omega_j) and can be of that order, while ||B_j|| ||B_j^{-1}|| = kappa_2(B_j) stays bounded: e.g. Lambda_1 = diag(1, 1+eta) with eta = 1/t, Omega_1 = [[1,0],[t,1]] gives B_1 = [[1,0],[1,1+eta]] with kappa_2(B_1) = O(1), but the first ratio equals t. So the displayed inequality is false. The accompanying equality is false as well, since kappa_2 is not a similarity invariant: B-hat_1 = (B_1-B_2)^{-1}B_1(B_1-B_2) is only similar to B_1 and ||B-hat_1|| ||B-hat_1^{-1}|| differs from ||B_1|| ||B_1^{-1}|| in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display by the correct estimate chi_mono <= max_i ||Omega_i|| ||Omega_i^{-1}|| for d=2 (more generally max_{k,i} kappa(Omega_i^{(k)} S_{i,d}^{(k)})), and drop the similarity-invariance claim for kappa_2; the conclusion that chi_mono is controllable by random matrix theory is then immediate.
issues.overall_effect: The worked-out d=2 case misrepresents the quantity controlling the growth of the fundamental matrix polynomials: chi_mono is governed by the conditioning of the eigenvector matrices Omega_i (and their S_{i,d}-transformed versions), not by cond(B_i); the surrounding claim that chi_mono is accessible to random-matrix estimates survives only with the corrected expression.
issues.title: The d=2 illustration bounds chi_mono by a false expression in terms of cond(B_i)
issues.why_classification: The substantive claim of the passage (chi_mono is bounded by random-matrix quantities) survives with a short local correction of the expression; no theorem, rate or regime changes and no new argument is needed.
